title: Establishment and evaluation of a structured, multidisciplinary, guideline-based transition and (long-term) aftercare for children and adolescents formerly affected by cancer
summary:
In Germany, approximately 2,100 children and adolescents up to the age of 18 are diagnosed with cancer every year. Despite good long-term survival rates, many of these patients are affected by late effects of the oncological disease and therapy. They therefore require long-term follow-up care to minimize the spread of secondary diseases.
The main objective of the study is to establish a long-term aftercare program based on official scientific guidelines. It will be investigated whether this leads to an improved care of children and adolescents with cancer, combined with a higher self-efficacy of the affected persons and their parents.
In order to compare the current aftercare with a holistic, guideline-oriented aftercare, the affected persons, their parents and experts will be asked in qualitative interviews about their experiences, wishes and expectations of the long-term aftercare. In an online survey - in cooperation with the Techniker Krankenkasse - the needs and experiences with the previous aftercare in a group of young, formerly cancer-affected adults will also be asked and the self-efficacy, quality of life and general health of the participants will also be examined. The results of these two study sections will be incorporated into a study section in which the improved aftercare will be compared with the standard aftercare in a total of ten study centers in Germany. This will be followed by an evaluation of the measures through interviews with patients, parents and experts who participated in the study. 
It is expected that the improved long-term aftercare will prevent overuse, underuse and misuse of care for former children and adolescents with cancer. By taking into account both medical and psychosocial aspects in the improved aftercare, the development of psychosocial late effects should thus also be avoided. Increased self-efficacy among parents and affected individuals should strengthen the willingness of affected families, children and adolescents to transition to adult medicine and to pursue lifelong follow-up care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Qualitative interviews prior to the start of the intervention:
- Written informed consent for the study
- In follow-up (patients)/active (staff).

Online interview:
- Age: minimum 18, maximum 39 years
- At least 5 years after end of treatment
- Identification via ICD-10 codes / OPS codes / ATC codes / EBM-GOPs.

RCT:
- Children and adolescents under 21 and one parent
- Regular oncology follow-up completed prior to intervention initiation

Qualitative interviews for intervention evaluation:
- Written informed consent for the study
- In follow-up as part of the RCT (patients)/working (staff)
Exclusion criteria:
Qualitative interviews prior to the start of the intervention:
- Insufficient knowledge of German
- Unknown time of therapy completion (patients)
- No written informed consent for the study

Online survey:
- Age: <18 years, >39 years
- End of treatment less than 5 years ago
- No malignant tumor disease

RCT:
- Individuals 21 years of age or older
- Patients in current oncological treatment
- Relocation within the intervention period expected
- No written informed consent for the study

Qualitative interviews for intervention evaluation:
- Insufficient knowledge of German
- No written informed consent for the study
